content.title: What are BufferedReader and BufferedWriter?
content.description: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter are Java classes that improve file reading and writing performance by using an internal buffer, reducing the number of direct disk operations.

content.content: Reading or writing one character at a time can be slow because each operation accesses the file system. BufferedReader and BufferedWriter use an internal memory buffer to process data efficiently, making file operations faster and more suitable for large files.

content.title: Why Use Buffered Streams?
content.content: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter reduce disk access, improve performance, and provide convenient methods for reading and writing text files.
BufferedReader reads text efficiently by buffering characters from an input stream. It also provides the convenient readLine() method for reading an entire line at once.

content.title: BufferedReader Example
Key Feature
content.description: The readLine() method reads an entire line of text, making BufferedReader simpler and faster than reading characters individually.

content.content: BufferedWriter writes characters efficiently by storing data temporarily in a buffer before writing it to the file.

content.title: BufferedWriter Example
Important Note
content.content: Always close or flush a BufferedWriter to ensure all buffered data is written to the file.
The flush() method forces all buffered output to be written immediately without closing the stream.

content.title: Water Storage Tank
content.content: Instead of fetching one bucket of water at a time, a storage tank collects a large amount and supplies it whenever needed. Similarly, buffered streams process data in batches to improve performance.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers commonly ask the differences between FileReader and BufferedReader, FileWriter and BufferedWriter, the purpose of buffering, readLine(), flush(), and when buffered streams should be preferred.

items.question: What happens if BufferedWriter is not closed?
items.answer: Some buffered data may never be written to the file.

items.question: Should BufferedReader always wrap another Reader?
items.answer: Yes. It wraps another Reader such as FileReader.

items.question: Is flush() the same as close()?
items.answer: No. flush() writes buffered data, while close() flushes the data and releases system resources.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter improve file I/O performance by using an internal buffer. BufferedReader is optimized for reading, while BufferedWriter is optimized for writing.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: BufferedReader improves reading performance using a buffer.
BufferedWriter improves writing performance using a buffer.
readLine() reads an entire line of text.
flush() writes buffered data without closing the stream.
Always close buffered streams after use.
Buffered streams are recommended for large text files.
